content.title: About
content.content: The Double Cheeseburger from McDonalds is a classic fast‑food sandwich made of two beef patties, two slices of Cheddar cheese, pickles, onions, mustard and ketchup, all sandwiched between a soft sesame‑seed bun. The item has been on the menu for over 20 years and is one of the most popular cheese‑lover choices.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: The Double Cheeseburger was introduced in the United States in the early 1990s as an extension of the original cheeseburger.
In Russia the product is often simply called “double cheeseburger” without the brand name, though it is officially sold only in McDonalds restaurants.
Each patty weighs about 45 g, giving the whole burger a total weight of roughly 200 g.
The recipe may vary slightly between countries due to local regulations and taste preferences.
The burger is served in McDonalds’ signature cardboard wrapper, which is easily recyclable.

items.title: Protein source
items.content: Two beef patties provide about 20 g of protein, supporting muscle maintenance.

items.title: Calcium from cheese
items.content: Cheddar cheese adds calcium, important for bone and tooth health.

items.title: B‑vitamins
items.content: Beef is rich in B12 and B6 vitamins, essential for energy metabolism and nervous system function.

items.title: Iron
items.content: Red meat supplies heme iron, which is more readily absorbed than plant‑based iron.

items.title: Energy boost
items.content: The combination of protein, fat and carbohydrates provides quick, sustained energy.

items.title: High calories and saturated fat
items.content: One Double Cheeseburger contains roughly 450–500 kcal and over 20 g of saturated fat, which can contribute to weight gain if eaten frequently.

items.title: Sodium content
items.content: Ketchup, mustard and pickles make the sandwich fairly salty (≈900 mg sodium), which may be problematic for hypertension.

items.title: Allergens
items.content: The product contains milk, gluten (bun) and soy (in some sauces), which can trigger allergic reactions.

items.title: Preservatives and additives
items.content: In some markets the patties include preservatives and flavor enhancers that may be undesirable for sensitive individuals.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: The burger is typically eaten hot, holding the bottom bun to avoid burning your hands. It pairs well with fries, a dipping sauce, or a soft drink. For a healthier twist, add fresh lettuce, tomato or other vegetables.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Freshly prepared burgers should be consumed immediately. If you need to store them, wrap tightly in foil and keep refrigerated for up to 24 hours. Reheat in a microwave or oven to restore bun crispness.
